state.project: Circuit OS: AI hardware compiler (plain English -> validated circuit, SPICE, KiCad, compiled firmware, BOM, graded claims). Phase 2 (Validation Engine) Stage 6 in progress; Phase 3 (Industrial Layer, PCB via freerouting + constraint layer) next.
project_invariants: The LLM writes only IntentIR (the requirement); deterministic generators write CircuitIR, SPICE, KiCad and firmware.
AI calls use forced tool_use; X5 retry rules; patches edit requirements only (RFC 6902 over IntentIR, X2/X4).
ngspice runs via Celery only; the MCU is modelled in SPICE as a resistor.
An accepted design never carries a failing claim; a claim's grade derives from its method only (G0..G7).
A generator VERSION change makes signed designs return 409 generator_changed until re-patched.
Pricing is static with price_asof; pricing never gates validation; live pricing (X7) needs the owner's explicit approval.
Jev's answer never overrides these rules or any project gate.
state.team: One engineer (the owner). No oscilloscope or signal generator; bench work only when the owner chooses. OpenRouter LLM credits exhausted as of 2026-09-23.

decision.question: Should the rs485_node generator add a 10 kOhm pull-down from the transceiver DE/RE net to GND?
decision.history: Raised during Phase 2 as a product call the owner kept. It keeps a rebooting node's driver off the bus (MCU pins float during reset) and could let the fail-safe claim stop citing D2 (MCU is a simplified model).

facts.fact: Topology U1 pin D2 drives the MAX485/MAX3485 DE and /RE pins together; PIN_DE_RE = 'D2'.
Claims on the design: rs485.failsafe_bias (monotone corners), driver_load, termination_dissipation, rail_current; D2 is cited per claim where the real MCU can reach it.
D2 register text: nothing in Phase 2 is scheduled to close it.
Added idle current when DE/RE is driven high: 5 V / 10 kOhm = 0.5 mA on Uno; 3.3 V / 10 kOhm = 0.33 mA on 3.3 V boards.
Changing the default output means rs485_node 0.2.0 -> version bump -> every signed RS-485 design returns 409 until re-patched.
M1 seeded-fault margin on this generator is thin: a 5% component fault moves V_AB by 2.3% against a 2% gate.
<PASTE: DE/RE pin (D2 / its ESP32 and STM32 equivalents) strapping or reserved status from data/mcu_targets.py and pin_rules on all 3 boards>
<PASTE: D7 figure record, or 'stated assumption', for MAX485/MAX3485 driver state while DE/RE floats during MCU reset>

options.what_changes: Every new RS-485 design gets R4 10k DE/RE->GND; generator version bump.
options.benefits: Reboot contention removed by default; possible D2 drop on fail-safe claim.
options.costs: Signed RS-485 designs invalidated (409); one more part; 0.33-0.5 mA idle.

reversibility.how_to_undo: Remove R4 and bump again; signatures already invalidated stay invalidated.

options.what_changes: constraints.de_re_pulldown (default false) adds R4 when set.
options.benefits: Users on multi-drop buses get it; existing designs byte-identical.
options.costs: Another constraint to test and document.

reversibility.how_to_undo: Remove the constraint; no signed design changed.

options.what_changes: Nothing now; record trigger: first multi-drop bus or first flashed RS-485 board.
options.costs: Risk stays for anyone who flashes a node on a shared bus.
Loses the option if the risk is real.

unknowns: How many users will put a node on a shared multi-drop bus in Phase 2/3.

pulldown_option.instructions: Which option should Circuit OS take for a DE/RE pull-down on the rs485_node generator?

criteria.add_as_default_now: Choose when the reboot-contention risk is material for most users and the cost of invalidating signed RS-485 designs is acceptable. Every new design gets R4; version bump.
criteria.add_as_opt_in_constraint: Choose when the benefit is real for some users but existing designs must stay byte-identical. constraints.de_re_pulldown defaults false; no signature impact.
criteria.defer_with_trigger: Choose when the risk only matters on multi-drop or flashed hardware not yet in use. Record trigger: first multi-drop bus or first flashed RS-485 board.
criteria.do_not_add: Choose when the state shows no material risk and the added part only costs.
criteria.need_more_information: Choose when a missing fact (pin status, transceiver reset behaviour) would change the answer.

reboot_contention_material.instructions: For a single-master Modbus RTU node on a bench or small bus, is a driver briefly enabled during MCU reset a material risk to other nodes' communication?

criteria.true: Material: plausible corrupted frames or bus lock on reboot.

reboot_contention_material__not.instructions: For a single-master Modbus RTU node on a bench or small bus, is a driver briefly enabled during MCU reset negligible for other nodes' communication?

d2_drop_is_sound.instructions: Given the state, would adding the pull-down remove the reason D2 (simplified MCU model) is cited on the fail-safe claim, rather than just moving it to another claim?

blast_radius.instructions: How far does the recommended change reach?
